fd_causeway_west.name: Fenmarch Causeway
fd_causeway_west.desc: Packed stone gives way to reed and standing water. Fenmarch's stilt-roofs show ahead through the reeds, gray on gray. West the causeway climbs back dry toward the Vale.
fd_causeway_west.brief: The causeway sinks into reed and water.

fd_north_dike.name: Fenmarch North Dike
fd_north_dike.desc: A raised dike holds the fen back from firmer ground. North the land climbs toward Hollowbrook's barrows; south the reeds close back over Reedholm's roofs.
fd_north_dike.brief: The dike holds back the fen.

fd_coast_road.name: Fenmarch Coast Road
fd_coast_road.desc: The road runs south on a spine of shingle between fen and open coast, salt creeping into the reed-smell. South it climbs toward the Saltkerns; north, Reedholm's stilts stand over black water.

fd_settlement.name: Reedholm — the Landing
fd_settlement.desc: Stilt-houses crowd over black water, gray planking strung rail to rail between them. Nets dry everywhere and nobody mends them. A causeway runs west, a dike north, a shingle road south; the settlement crowds east, and a boardwalk trails out into open reed.
fd_settlement.brief: Reedholm's landing, stilts over black water.
onEnterOnce: Somewhere past the last stilt-house, faint under the water at dusk, something sings. Nobody in Reedholm looks up when it does.

actions.label: listen to the water
fx: Voices, or near enough — layered, slow, more felt through the planking than heard. It stops the moment you're sure of it.

variants.desc: Stilt-houses crowd over black water, gray planking strung rail to rail between them. A length of black ribbon is tied to the landing rail, for hollows the Reach lost to fire this year. Nets dry everywhere and nobody mends them.
variants.brief: Reedholm's landing. A black ribbon on the rail.

fd_net_hall.name: The Net-Hall
fd_net_hall.desc: Long tables under a low roof, hung thick with nets that smell of tar and fish. A banked fire keeps the worst of the damp out. The eel-market lies north, the Priory south, the rest of Reedholm east; the landing is west.

actions.label: rest among the nets
fx: You sleep salt-damp and warm enough, rocked by the water under the planks.

actions.label: feed the letter to the banked fire
fx: The old paper catches fast and is ash before the words could trouble anyone further. Whatever the dead man meant to confess, the fire has it now instead of Reedholm.

variants.brief: Nets, a banked fire, and a driftwood-cart family warming through.
Nets, a banked fire, a driftwood-cart family keeping to the corner.

fd_eel_market.name: The Eel-Market
fd_eel_market.desc: Baskets of live eels hiss and slap in shallow tubs. A trader missing two fingers weighs catch against coin, calling prices to no one in particular. The net-hall lies south.
fd_eel_market.brief: Eels in tubs, a two-fingered scale.

actions.label: buy an eel-spear — 8 gold
fx: A long spear, barbed for eel-work and balanced well enough for worse. 'Mind the barb coming back out,' she says.

actions.label: buy an oilskin cloak — 6 gold
fx: Stiff with tar and salt, and it sheds water like it means it.

actions.label: buy smoked eel — 3 gold
fx: She wraps a length of smoked eel in waxed cloth without being asked twice.

actions.label: sell the corroded ward-coin
fx: She turns it over once, shrugs, and pays four coin for the curiosity of it.

fd_priory.name: The Priory of the Gray Church
fd_priory.desc: Stone among the stilts, older than Reedholm itself — the mother-house of the Gray Church, or what's left of it. Prior Halm keeps candles lit against the damp. A cloister leads east.

actions.label: press Halm on the tablet (will)
fx: He goes very still, then says it plain: they heard the bell-ringer's own warning and prayed over it instead. 'Now you know,' he says. 'Do with it what you will.'
He looks at the floor a long moment and won't be moved today — and something in how you pressed him will reach the Priory's own ears before you do.
He looks at the floor a long moment. 'Some things are between me and that water,' he says, and won't be moved past it today.

actions.label: loom over him until he breaks (might)
fx: You back him against the altar rail until the fear of you outweighs the fear of the water. 'Now you know,' he says, small. 'Do with it what you will.'
He goes rigid but says nothing, and you're not a man who beats confessions out of priests. Not today, anyway. It can be tried again.

actions.label: lay the tablet against his words (wits)
fx: You lay the tablet's scraped confession next to his own account of the flood and let the dates do the arguing. He can't refute his own hand. 'Now you know,' he says. 'Do with it what you will.'
The dates almost line up, not quite enough to pin him — and the Priory hears only that a stranger tried to build a case against its own Prior.
The dates almost line up, almost — not quite enough to pin him with. He watches you fail to make the case, and says nothing.

actions.label: tell Halm what the Ironbound mean to do
fx: Halm's face goes hard in a way you haven't seen on him. By evening the Priory's own men have walked the Ironbound off Stilt Row, iron sun and all. 'Not in my water,' is all he says of it.

fd_priory_cloister.name: The Cloister
fd_priory_cloister.desc: A covered walk rings a drowned garden, more mud than green now. Grave-tablets line the inner wall, names worn past reading — except one, kept clear of moss on purpose. The Priory lies west.
fd_priory_cloister.brief: The drowned garden, one clear tablet.

actions.label: read the one clear grave-tablet
fx: A name, a date — the flood's year — and beneath it, scraped by a different, later hand: THE DOOR STOOD OPEN. THEY CHOSE TO PRAY. Not a mason's line. Someone's confession, half-erased since.

actions.label: leave the letter with the grave-tablets
fx: You wedge the letter behind the one clear tablet. Whoever wrote it, and whoever it was for, Reedholm will remember them now, unnamed or not.

fd_stilt_row.name: Stilt Row
fd_stilt_row.desc: Leaning houses on stilts, walkways slick underfoot. A child's shoe hangs from one rail, small and gray, and nobody has taken it down in years. The net-hall lies west.
fd_stilt_row.brief: Leaning houses, a small gray shoe.

fd_drying_racks.name: The Drying Racks
fd_drying_racks.desc: Racks of split eel curing over a low fire. Whoever tends them has stepped away — a knife's stuck in the block, a coil of tarred rope beside it.
fd_drying_racks.brief: Curing eel, a knife left in the block.

actions.label: take the coil of tarred rope
fx: Good rope, tarred against the wet. Whoever left it isn't likely to miss one coil.

fd_ironbound_camp.name: The Ironbound Mission
fd_ironbound_camp.desc: A netshed requisitioned and hung with the Ironbound's iron sun. A brazier stays lit day and night. Two of them keep it, waiting on an order to burn the nave and be done with the singing.
fd_ironbound_camp.brief: A netshed, an iron sun, a lit brazier.

variants.desc: The netshed stands empty, the iron sun taken down. Ash from the brazier is the only sign they were ever here.

fd_way_shrine.name: The Wayside Shrine
fd_way_shrine.desc: A hump of dry ground beside the causeway, a gray-stone niche wedged with candle stubs. A shrine-keeper kneels by a pilgrim laid on a traveler's cloak, breath gone shallow and slow.
fd_way_shrine.brief: A candle-niche, a keeper, a dying pilgrim.
onEnterOnce: Word crossed the causeway days back: the Vale's king sleeps easier now. The keeper lit an extra candle for it.
Word crossed the causeway days back: the Vale's king fell to the blade. The keeper lights no extra candle for that kind of rest.
Word crossed the causeway days back: the Vale's king was left to his barrow, neither rested nor slain. The keeper only sighs at that.

actions.label: sit with the dying pilgrim (will)
fx: You find the words, low and plain, and hold their hand until the breath just stops, easier than it was. The keeper says nothing. Nothing needs saying.
You sit, but the words don't come, not the right ones. They go before you find them. The keeper closes the eyes for you, gently, like it's not the first time.

actions.label: offer to carry a token onward
fx: The keeper presses a small clay token into your hand, warm from the candle-niche. "Leave it at the next chapel's altar," they say. "Let the name travel that far."

fd_ford.name: The Washed Ford
fd_ford.desc: A plank footbridge that isn't, not since the spring flood took its middle third. What's left leans toward a channel running faster than fen water has any right to.
fd_ford.brief: A broken footbridge, a fast channel.
onEnterOnce: Ash rides the current down from Hollowbrook some mornings, thin and gray. Nobody at the dike has said why out loud.
The channel's run clearer since word came down that Hollowbrook's mound went quiet. Small mercies, this far from the mere.
Word came down that Hollowbrook bought its grief quiet. The channel doesn't care either way, but you do.

actions.label: force the ford — fail costs 2hp (might)
fx: You put your shoulder into the current and cross by main strength, plank or no plank. It's cold, and it's done.
The current wants you more than the far bank does. You claw back out, soaked and short some strength for it.

actions.label: cross the ford — fail costs 1hp (grace)
fx: You find the give in each plank before it finds you, and cross light-footed over the gap the flood left.
One plank answers your weight wrong, and you go down hard on the good one, winded.

actions.label: backtrack for the long way round
fx: You lose the better part of an hour finding a drier crossing upstream, but you cross dry, and that's worth something too.

fd_wayside_camp.name: The Drovers' Halt
fd_wayside_camp.desc: A hollow off the shingle, sheltered by dune-grass. A family has pulled a handcart off the road and built a low fire, penny-pinching driftwood, watching the coast road both ways.
fd_wayside_camp.brief: A driftwood fire, a handcart family.

variants.name: The Refugees' Halt
variants.desc: A hollow off the shingle, sheltered by dune-grass. A family sits close around a driftwood fire, what they carried out of a burned hold stacked small beside them — not much, and all of it.
variants.brief: A driftwood fire, a burned hold's family.

actions.label: share coin with the family
fx: You press coin into the mother's hand. She doesn't thank you in words — just holds it a moment like it's heavier than coin should be.
The drover nods you a real thanks and pockets it without counting. "Every hold pays a toll somewhere," he says. "Glad this one's kind."

actions.label: share food with the family
fx: You hand over what's left of your own rations. The children don't wait for permission before eating.
You share out your rations without being asked twice. The drover's wife insists on trading you a strip of dried meat for it anyway.

actions.label: turn them away
fx: You keep walking. Behind you, nobody calls out — they've learned better by now than to expect otherwise.
You keep walking. The drover doesn't call out either, just watches you go with the look of a man revising his opinion of strangers.

fd_smoked_eel.name: smoked eel
fd_smoked_eel.hint: eat it to ease a wound

fx: Salt and smoke; it settles the stomach and eases the ache.

fd_tarred_rope.name: coil of tarred rope
fd_tarred_rope.hint: good for hauling something heavy up out of black water

fd_pitch.name: skin of Ironbound pitch
fd_pitch.hint: the Ironbound's own brand-oil, meant for burning what won't rest

fd_shrine_token.name: the pilgrim's clay token
fd_shrine_token.hint: leave it at the next chapel's altar

fd_prior_candle.name: a fat altar candle, unlit
fd_prior_candle.hint: Church wax, meant for the drowned nave's altar

fd_trader_scale.name: a set of brass scale-weights
fd_trader_scale.hint: keeps the trader honest, or looks like it

fd_netkeep_needle.name: a bone net-needle
fd_netkeep_needle.hint: worth little except to someone who knows knots

fd_prior.name: Prior Halm
fd_prior.desc: A thin man in gray, hands never quite still, watching the water through the door as much as you.

topics.label: who are you
topics.say: Prior Halm, for what that's worth these days. Sit if the damp doesn't trouble you — it troubles everyone eventually, in Fenmarch.

topics.label: this Priory
topics.say: This is the Gray Church's mother-house — every gray priest between here and Coldpass trained under this roof once, mine included. Little enough to show for it now.

topics.label: the flood
topics.say: Twenty years gone, the water rose in a night and took the old nave and its whole congregation with it. We prayed instead of ringing the warning bell. I did not choose that. I was young enough not to be asked.

topics.label: what folk say about the flood
topics.say: Some in Reedholm say the Priory chose prayer over the bell on purpose, to test their faith. I've never found the courage to ask which of my elders believed that — or whether I would have.

topics.label: your novice, Brother Osk
topics.say: Sent to me green and hopeful, and I've taught him rites for a grief he had never stood in front of, not until you brought him this far east. I owe him better than I've given him.

topics.label: the Ironbound on Stilt Row
topics.say: Two of the Ironbound have pitched camp on Stilt Row, waiting to burn the nave and be done with it. They aren't wrong that something must be done. I only wish they'd asked before they arrived.

topics.label: the singing's stopped
topics.say: I felt it go, like a held breath finally let out. Whatever you did down there, it was mercy, and Fenmarch will not forget it soon.

topics.label: the tithe you promised
topics.say: Quieter, they tell me, not gone. A tithe's not absolution, but it's honest dealing, and the water seems to have taken it as such. I can live with quieter.

topics.label: the fire on the water
topics.say: You burned them. I understand the reasoning — I may even understand the mercy in it — but I buried my own faith in that water once, and now there's nothing left down there to visit.

topics.label: word of a hollow at rest
topics.say: Halm hears it secondhand, the way he hears most things now, and still it reaches him.
fx: "Another hold rested its grief instead of burning it," he says, hands finally still. "Then it can be done gently. Good."

topics.label: leave the pilgrim's token at the altar
topics.say: Halm takes the token without a word and sets it among the others on the sill. "One more name the water didn't get to keep quiet," he says. "My thanks for carrying it."

topics.label: word of a robbed crypt
topics.say: Word travels a Church roof faster than you'd think. However it happened, wherever, a crypt robbed is a crypt robbed. That doesn't sit easy with me.

topics.label: word of the dead well kept
topics.say: You've a habit of leaving the dead better than you found them. That's rarer than you'd think, and the Church remembers who does it. Take this — small, but it's meant.

topics.label: leave him to his candles
topics.say: Go gently on the walkways. Reedholm loses someone to the water most years; I'd rather not add a name I know.

topics.label: about the altar candle, since
topics.say: Halm counts the candles now before he counts the collection plate. "Take from the drowned's own altar, and pray to them yourself next time," he says.

fd_sexton.name: old sexton
fd_sexton.desc: Bent low over the one clear tablet, scraping moss that keeps coming back.

topics.label: the tablet you keep clear
topics.say: Someone has to. The rest can go under the moss; that one, never. It isn't for the dead's sake I keep it — it's for the Priory's memory, which is shorter.

topics.label: what happened, the year of the flood
topics.say: The water rose faster than anyone thought it could, and the Priory prayed instead of ringing the bell to run. Halm wasn't Prior then. He was young, and he watched it happen.

fd_netkeep.name: netkeep
fd_netkeep.desc: Mending net by firelight, fingers quick despite the poor light.

topics.label: the hall
topics.say: Warm, dry-ish, and nobody drowns under this roof. That's the whole of what I promise anyone. Steer clear of the old Flood-Watch tower past the reeds; it leans worse every year.

topics.label: what folk are saying
topics.say: That the singing's gotten louder since the Ironbound pitched their camp on Stilt Row. Whether that's the water answering them or just Reedholm's nerves, I couldn't say.

topics.label: the driftwood-cart family
topics.say: The netkeep nods toward the corner where they've settled.
fx: "Word reached us a stranger shared coin and bread with them on the coast road. That's why they trust this roof enough to stay," the netkeep says.
"They don't say much about the coast road," the netkeep says. "Whatever happened out there, it's why they watch the door more than the fire."

topics.label: the smoke over the water
topics.say: I've mended nets under worse skies. Never one I helped make, though.

topics.label: about the net-needle, since
topics.say: He pats down the hall's tools before you're even out of sight now. "Word doesn't travel free to hands that don't ask first," he says.

fd_eel_trader.name: eel-trader
fd_eel_trader.desc: Two fingers gone at the second knuckle, and quick enough with the rest not to miss them.

topics.label: the trade
topics.say: Eels don't care whose water they're in. Been a leaner catch since something's been tearing my traps out past the reed-line — near the Eel-Run some nights, just as often nowhere close to it.

topics.label: the traps somebody's tearing out
topics.say: Something with more strength than sense, out in the reeds. Bring me proof of what's doing it and there's coin in it — three or four.

topics.label: the hide, for the bounty
topics.say: That's the hide, all right. Ugly thing. Here — and my traps thank you, even if they can't say so themselves.
fx: She counts four coins into your palm without haggling, which from her is its own kind of thanks.

topics.label: the eel-trap charm, for the bounty
topics.say: Not what's tearing my traps — different bite, different drag. But you went out for my sake and came back with something. That's worth a coin or two.
fx: She counts out two coins, slower than she did for the hide. 'For the trying,' she says. 'Not for the eel.'

topics.label: the Ironbound on Stilt Row
topics.say: Bad for business, zealots. Folk don't linger to buy eel with a brazier and a burning-sermon two doors down.

topics.label: the smell of the eel-market
topics.say: Tubs and brine, morning to night. You get used to it, or you don't stay.

topics.label: about the scale-weights, since
topics.say: She's counted her weights twice since. "Fingers that quick don't get my good prices anymore," she says, and means it.

fd_mara.name: Mara
fd_mara.desc: Hangs washing that never quite dries, watching the water more than the line.

topics.label: who are you
topics.say: Lived on this row longer than most of the houses have stood. My husband went out checking eel-traps the night of the flood, twenty years gone. Never came back to be buried.

topics.label: ask about her husband
topics.say: If you go down there — if you find anything of his, a ring, a boot-buckle, anything — I'd want to know. Even now. Especially now.

topics.label: tell her what the water gave up
topics.say: You set the buckle in her hands, black with years underwater. She holds it a long moment, then nods, like a question finally answered. 'Twenty years,' she says. 'I can stop asking now.'

topics.label: tell her he's at peace
topics.say: You tell her he's at peace, though you found nothing of him at all. She wants to believe it badly enough that she does. It isn't the truth. It settles her all the same.

topics.label: how she's getting on
topics.say: Better, some days. The row's quieter without the wondering in it. Thank you for that, whichever way you managed it.

topics.label: leave her to the washing
topics.say: Mind the planks past the third house. They've been rotten for years.

fd_ironbound_warder.name: Warder Iss
fd_ironbound_warder.desc: An iron sun on a cord at her throat, watching the water like it owes her something.

topics.label: who are you
topics.say: Ironbound, out of Cinderhall. That nave's been singing grief into this water for a hundred years and the Church has done nothing but pray at it. We don't pray. We finish things.

topics.label: the order you're waiting on
topics.say: Preceptor's word, or our own patience running out first. Either way, that nave burns eventually. Help us do it clean and it goes easier on everyone in these stilts.

topics.label: side with them: take their pitch
topics.say: Now you're talking sense. Take it — and when you're standing over that water, remember whose fire you're carrying.

topics.label: tell her the Church handles its own dead
topics.say: Your funeral, not ours — but then, everything down here already is somebody's funeral. Suit yourself.

topics.label: the nave, now it's settled
topics.say: Quiet, is it. Wasn't fire, but quiet's something. We'll take word of it back to Cinderhall regardless — a hollow dealt with is a hollow dealt with, our way or not.

topics.label: word from Cinderhall
topics.say: A courier off the coast road brings news from the chapterhouse.
fx: "Their own Preceptor, thrown out by his own chapterhouse." Iss's jaw goes tight. "Then the order polices its own house before it lectures mine."

topics.label: leave the mission to its brazier
topics.say: Mind the water. It remembers who prayed and who didn't.

fd_ironbound_second.name: the second zealot
fd_ironbound_second.desc: Feeds the brazier without being told to, and watches you over the flame.

topics.label: say nothing, just look at him
topics.say: He doesn't look up from the fire. 'Warder does the talking,' he says, and goes back to feeding it.

fd_perrins_mother.name: Perrin's mother
fd_perrins_mother.desc: Watches the causeway more than the water, a boy's bedding still folded on the shelf.

topics.label: who keeps this vigil at the landing
topics.say: Perrin's mother, is who. My boy went to pay a debt in the Watch's colors, two winters gone to Highward. I keep his bed made up regardless.

topics.label: ask after her son at Highward
topics.say: If you're bound for Wardmoor, ask the barracks after Perrin. Tell me true, whatever you find. I'd rather know than keep hoping blind.

topics.label: tell her what became of Perrin
topics.say: She's been watching the causeway every evening since you asked.
fx: She doesn't wait for you to finish the sentence before she's moving — down the road, toward whatever's coming.
"Steadier, not home," she says, and nods like that's the better mercy. "I can live with steadier."
She goes very quiet, then thanks you for the truth of it, which is not the same as thanking you for the news.

topics.label: tell her you've no word yet
topics.say: She only nods, the way she's nodded every evening for two winters. "Bed's still made," she says.

epilogue.text: The Priory prays a name for every hold's grief it hears was rested, and burns a candle, not a nave, for every one that wasn't.
The wayside shrine's keeper still tells travelers of the stranger who sat with a dying pilgrim rather than just walk on.
Travelers on the coast road still speak of a stranger who shared what little they had with a family on the road.
One more name rests among the Priory's grave-tablets now, carried east by a stranger, unread by anyone else.
A dead man's letter went into Reedholm's banked fire, unread. Whatever he meant to confess, the ash keeps it now.
A sealed letter went down into the drowned nave's black water, joining a grief it never asked to keep.
The pilgrim's token reached the Priory altar after all, one more name the water didn't keep quiet.
Travelers on the coast road still speak of a stranger who looked a hungry family over and kept walking.

stages.text: You're in Wardmoor. Ask after Perrin at Highward's barracks.
A Reedholm mother wants word of her son, pressed into the Watch at Highward, in Wardmoor.
